title: Roma
description: Roma (Roma (Rome)) - Capital of the Roman Empire; supreme hub of all Italian road networks. Origin point of the Milliarium Aureum (Golden Milestone).

title: Ostia
description: Ostia (Ostia Antica) - Principal harbour of Rome at the Tiber mouth; key node for maritime-to-terrestrial traffic transfer. Via Ostiensis terminus.

title: Capua
description: Capua (Santa Maria Capua Vetere) - Most important city of Campania; major junction on the Via Appia and Via Latina; key military and commercial hub.

title: Neapolis
description: Neapolis (Napoli (Naples)) - Largest Greek-founded city in Campania; important cultural and commercial centre. Connected to Capua and Puteoli by road.

title: Puteoli
description: Puteoli (Pozzuoli) - Major port on the Bay of Naples; chief harbour for eastern Mediterranean trade until Ostia expanded under Claudius.

title: Herculaneum
description: Herculaneum (Ercolano) - Prosperous Campanian coastal town; destroyed 79 CE (Vesuvius). Included as representative Campanian road-network node.

title: Nola
description: Nola (Nola) - Ancient Oscan and Roman colony; important road junction east of Neapolis linking Campania to Apulia.

title: Pompeii
description: Pompeii (Pompei) - Prosperous Roman town destroyed 79 CE; well-documented road connections along the Campanian coastal route.

title: Brundisium
description: Brundisium (Brindisi) - Terminus of the Via Appia and Via Traiana; primary embarkation point for Greece and the Eastern Mediterranean. Key strategic port.

title: Tarentum
description: Tarentum (Taranto) - Major Greek colony turned Roman municipium; important harbour on the Gulf of Taranto. Junction of routes through southern Italy.

title: Venusia
description: Venusia (Venosa) - Latin colony on Via Appia; strategic crossroads between Apulia and Lucania. Birthplace of Horace.

title: Luceria
description: Luceria (Lucera) - Important Latin colony in northern Apulia; road junction on routes through the Apennine passes toward the Adriatic.

title: Rhegium
description: Rhegium (Reggio Calabria) - Greek colony at the tip of Italy; southern terminus of the Via Popilia; embarkation point for Sicily. Extreme southern road endpoint.

title: Consentia
description: Consentia (Cosenza) - Chief Bruttian city; important road junction on the Via Popilia through the toe of Italy toward Rhegium.

title: Heraclea
description: Heraclea (Policoro) - Greek and Lucanian city on the Ionian coast; junction linking coastal Lucanian route with interior roads.

title: Beneventum
description: Beneventum (Benevento) - Critical road junction: meeting point of Via Appia, Via Traiana, and Via Latina. Major Samnite and Roman colony.

title: Aesernia
description: Aesernia (Isernia) - Latin colony in Samnium; important strategic garrison point controlling interior Apennine routes.

title: Ancona
description: Ancona (Ancona) - Major Adriatic port; northern terminus of the Via Flaminia. Junction linking Adriatic coastal traffic to interior.

title: Asculum Picenum
description: Asculum Picenum (Ascoli Piceno) - Principal city of Picenum; road junction on routes connecting the Adriatic coast to the Apennine interior.

title: Spoletium
description: Spoletium (Spoleto) - Key colony on the Via Flaminia between Rome and Ariminum. Important military road junction controlling the Apennine pass.

title: Narnia
description: Narnia (Narni) - Latin colony on the Via Flaminia immediately north of Rome; first major stop on the road north.

title: Iguvium
description: Iguvium (Gubbio) - Important Umbrian city; road junction connecting the Via Flaminia to secondary routes through northern Umbria.

title: Florentia
description: Florentia (Firenze (Florence)) - Roman colony at a key Arno river crossing; road junction connecting Via Cassia and Via Flaminia corridors.

title: Arretium
description: Arretium (Arezzo) - Major Etruscan and Roman city; junction on the Via Cassia with roads east to Umbrrian towns. Important ceramic production centre.

title: Perusia
description: Perusia (Perugia) - Major Etruscan city and Roman municipium; road junction linking Etruria to Umbria across the Tiber valley.

title: Pisae
description: Pisae (Pisa) - Coastal Etruscan and Roman city; important harbour at the Arno mouth on the Via Aurelia corridor.

title: Bononia
description: Bononia (Bologna) - Major junction on the Via Aemilia; principal road city of Cisalpine Gaul crossing the Apennines toward Etruria.

title: Mutina
description: Mutina (Modena) - Latin colony on the Via Aemilia; key road centre in the Po plain between Bononia and Placentia.

title: Parma
description: Parma (Parma) - Latin colony on the Via Aemilia; important road and commercial node in the Po plain.

title: Placentia
description: Placentia (Piacenza) - Latin colony at the terminus of the Via Aemilia on the Po; major junction connecting to Mediolanum, Genua, and Cremona.

title: Ariminum
description: Ariminum (Rimini) - Latin colony at the junction of Via Flaminia (from Rome) and Via Aemilia (north-west); strategic road node on the Adriatic.

title: Genua
description: Genua (Genova (Genoa)) - Major Ligurian port; junction of coastal Via Aurelia and interior routes over the Apennines toward Placentia (Via Postumia).

title: Alba Pompeia
description: Alba Pompeia (Alba) - Ligurian Roman colony; road junction in the Tanaro valley connecting the Po plain with Alpine routes.

title: Aquileia
description: Aquileia (Aquileia) - Critical northeastern gateway of Italy; major road hub connecting Italy to the Balkans, Danube frontier, and the Amber Road.

title: Verona
description: Verona (Verona) - Major road junction on the Adige; connecting Via Postumia with routes north through the Brenner Pass toward Raetia.

title: Patavium
description: Patavium (Padova (Padua)) - Wealthy Venetian city on the Via Postumia; one of the most prosperous cities in Roman Italy.

title: Tergeste
description: Tergeste (Trieste) - Important Adriatic port and road junction near Aquileia; gateway to Histria and the Dalmatian coast.

title: Cremona
description: Cremona (Cremona) - Latin colony on the Po; road junction on Via Postumia linking Genua to Aquileia through the Po plain.

title: Mediolanum
description: Mediolanum (Milano (Milan)) - Capital of Transpadana; supreme road hub of northern Italy connecting routes to all Alpine passes and major Po plain cities. Later imperial capital of the West.

title: Augusta Taurinorum
description: Augusta Taurinorum (Torino (Turin)) - Roman colony at the foot of the Alps; road junction controlling Mont Cenis and Little St. Bernard passes into Gaul.

title: Ticinum
description: Ticinum (Pavia) - Road junction on the Ticino river; connecting Mediolanum with Placentia and routes south across the Apennines.

title: Novaria
description: Novaria (Novara) - Road junction between Mediolanum and Augusta Taurinorum; controlling western Transpadana.

title: Corfinium
description: Corfinium (Corfinio) - Capital of the Italian allies during the Social War (91–87 BCE); interior road junction in the central Apennines. Pleiades ID: 413063.

title: Cales
description: Cales (Calvi Risorta) - Important Latin colony on the Via Latina corridor between Rome and Capua; wine-producing region.

title: Buxentum
description: Buxentum (Policastro Bussentino) - Latin colony on the Tyrrhenian coast of Lucania; road node on the coastal route between Campania and Bruttium.
